statements.text: Experience is unified, bounded and differentiated, with a single subject, and it is hard to see how many microphysical systems with their own (proto)phenomenal properties could add up to it, rather than to a jagged collection of phenomenal spikes. It can be put as a conceivability argument: micro quiddities seem possible without any macro experience. Chalmers calls it the most serious problem for the view, and many regard it as unsolved.

sources.quote: Should one not expect something more like a disunified, jagged collection of phenomenal spikes?
I think it is easily the most serious problem for the type-F monist view
One way to pose the combination problem is in the form of a conceivability argument.
many regard the combination problem for Russellian monism as unsolved and serious
